cdsListItem.cdsListItemValue: Cholera not routine; see ACIP/Yellow Book

outboundCoding.displayName: Supplemental text is available for this recommendation.
outboundCoding.originalText: Cholera vaccination is not routinely recommended in the U.S. and only indicated for select patients at increased risk. Refer to ACIP and the CDC Yellow Book: Health Information for International Travel for additional information.

cdsListItem.cdsListItemValue: PCV20/21 via SCDM >=5y after last pneumococcal

outboundCoding.displayName: Supplemental text is available for this recommendation.
outboundCoding.originalText: Consider administering PCV20 or PCV21 based on Shared Clinical Decision-Making (SCDM), at least 5 years after the most recent dose of pneumococcal vaccine.

cdsListItem.cdsListItemValue: If no PPSV23, use PCV20/21; then stop

outboundCoding.displayName: Supplemental text is available for this recommendation.
outboundCoding.originalText: If PPSV23 is unavailable, PCV20 or PCV21 may be administered. No further doses of any type of pneumococcal vaccine are recommended after PCV20 or PCV21 is given.

cdsListItem.cdsListItemValue: Maternal unvacc/unknown/within 14d: give RSV mAb

outboundCoding.displayName: Supplemental text is available for this recommendation.
outboundCoding.originalText: If the mother of the patient was not vaccinated during her pregnancy, her vaccination status is unknown, or she was vaccinated within 14 days of the patient date of birth, then administer RSV mAb dose based on patient weight shortly before or during the RSV season.

cdsListItem.cdsListItemValue: JE not routine; accel schedule 18-65; see ACIP

outboundCoding.displayName: Supplemental text is available for this recommendation.
outboundCoding.originalText: Japanese Encephalitis vaccination is not routinely recommended in the U.S. and only indicated for select patients at increased risk. The only age group for which an accelerated schedule is approved is 18-65 years old. Refer to ACIP and the CDC Yellow Book: Health Information for International Travel for additional information.

cdsListItem.cdsListItemValue: After 3-dose monovalent: 1 bivalent booster >=8w

outboundCoding.displayName: Supplemental text is available for this recommendation.
outboundCoding.originalText: Patients who previously completed a 3-dose monovalent primary series are recommended to receive 1 bivalent booster dose, at least 8 weeks after completion of the monovalent primary series.

cdsListItem.cdsListItemValue: Adult risk: PCV20/21 or PCV15 then PPSV23

outboundCoding.displayName: Supplemental text is available for this recommendation.
outboundCoding.originalText: The Pneumococcal evaluations and recommendations in ICE primarily target the routine series. Adults ages 19-49 with underlying medical conditions or other risk factors who have not previously received PCV or whose previous vaccination history is unknown should receive 1 dose of PCV (either PCV20, PCV21 or PCV15). When PCV15 is used, it should be followed by a dose of PPSV23 at the appropriate interval(s). Patients who previously received a PCV13 should receive PCV20 or PCV21. Refer to ACIP for additional information.

cdsListItem.cdsListItemValue: RSV: single lifetime dose (75+; 50-74 at risk)

outboundCoding.displayName: Supplemental text is available for this recommendation.
outboundCoding.originalText: The RSV evaluations and recommendations in ICE primarily target the routine series. RSV is recommended as a single lifetime dose for all adults 75 years of age and older and adults 50 through 74 years of age and older who are at increased risk of severe RSV disease. Note: RSV vaccine is also recommended for pregnant persons at 32 through 36 weeks gestation, using seasonal administration.

cdsListItem.cdsListItemValue: RSV: 75+ or 50-74 at risk

outboundCoding.displayName: Supplemental text is available for this recommendation.
outboundCoding.originalText: The RSV evaluations and recommendations in ICE primarily target the routine series. RSV is recommended as a single lifetime dose for all adults 75 years of age and older and adults 50 through 74 years of age who are at increased risk of severe RSV disease.

cdsListItem.cdsListItemValue: Target dose 1: Novavax 3w; others 8-12w

outboundCoding.displayName: Supplemental text is available for this recommendation.
outboundCoding.originalText: The interval to target dose 1 depends on the patient's prior history and product to be used. If the last shot was an updated Novavax, Novavax can be administered in 3 weeks (as long as the patient is 12 years of age). If the last shot was not Novavax, administer at an interval of 8 weeks (for administration of Comirnaty, Novavax, or Spikevax) or 12 weeks (for administration of mNEXSPIKE).

cdsListItem.cdsListItemValue: Target dose 1: Novavax 3w; others 8-12w

outboundCoding.displayName: Supplemental text is available for this recommendation.
outboundCoding.originalText: The interval to target dose 1 depends on the patient's prior history and product to be used. If the last shot was an updated Novavax, Novavax can be administered in 3 weeks. If the last shot was not Novavax, administer at an interval of 8 weeks (for administration of Comirnaty, Novavax, or Spikevax) or 12 weeks (for administration of mNEXSPIKE).

cdsListItem.cdsListItemValue: Target dose 2: rec 6mo; min 8-12w by product

outboundCoding.displayName: Supplemental text is available for this recommendation.
outboundCoding.originalText: The recommended interval to target dose 2 is 6 months. The minimum interval to target dose 2 depends on the product to be used. For administration of Comirnaty, Novavax, or Spikevax, minimum interval = 8 weeks. For administration of mNEXSPIKE, minimum interval = 12 weeks.

cdsListItem.cdsListItemValue: Yellow fever: live; min 24/28/30d; see ACIP

outboundCoding.displayName: Supplemental text is available for this recommendation.
outboundCoding.originalText: Yellow fever vaccination is not routinely recommended in the U.S. and is only indicated for select patients at increased risk. Yellow fever is a live vaccine. An absolute minimum interval of 24 days is required between yellow fever vaccines. An absolute minimum interval of 28 days is required between a yellow fever vaccine and a live vaccine from another vaccine group. The minimum and recommended interval between yellow fever and another live vaccine is 30 days. Refer to ACIP and the CDC Yellow Book: Health Information for International Travel for additional information.
